title: Hyperserial tool bridge with signal stops and result pinning
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Implement a new "hyperserial" tool bridge that enables reliable multi-tool chaining across streaming responses, structured output contracts, and compatibility layers while preventing runaway recursion and loops. This work tightens how tool results are injected back into the model context, how streaming frames are annotated for provenance, and how the runtime stops/pauses tool chains when safety conditions are hit.

Goals:
- Provide a single, consistent streaming envelope for mixed model+tool traffic that preserves provenance (tool_id, run_id, token_offset) for downstream consumers and the console.
- Implement an execution sentinel system (signal stops) that can: (a) gracefully stop a chain, (b) pause and request human review, or (c) convert to a fallback runner when a recursion pattern is detected.
- Ensure idempotent result injection so retries and duplicate tool responses do not corrupt the chat/history state.
- Build a compact compatibility shim for older tool contracts (v1) so we can route between new structured outputs (v2 schema) and legacy consumers without breakage.

Design notes / decisions made so far:
- Streaming envelope: we use a simple top-level frame with fields encoded as text: FRAME_TYPE|SEQ|RUN_ID|PROV=tool:tool_id;run:run_id|PAYLOAD=... The runtime converts this to structured records in telemetry and the console. This avoids breaking existing SDKs that expect newline-delimited chunks.
- Signal stops: three levels of sentinel are defined as strings: STOP_IMMEDIATE, STOP_PAUSE_REVIEW, STOP_FALLBACK. These are implemented as metadata in the frame stream and evaluated by the orchestrator synchronously.
- Recursion detection heuristics: we use a combination of (1) direct call graph depth limit (configurable per-customer, default 6), (2) repetition of the same tool_id+input fingerprint > 3 in a sliding window, and (3) a wall-clock TTL per tool run (default 4s). If any threshold trips, emit STOP_FALLBACK and increment telemetry counter.
- Idempotency: each tool invocation carries an idempotency_token (sha1 of tool_id + normalized_inputs + request_root_id). Tool results are applied only if the token is not already consumed in the session store. This prevents double-inject.
- Compatibility layer: v1->v2 shim lives in the orchestrator: we transform legacy freeform outputs to a minimal v2 wrapper with fields: schema_version, content_map, provenance. The shim is pluggable and can be disabled via feature flag.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Using a text-delimited streaming envelope keeps SDK compatibility but forces extra parse work in runtimes; alternative was protobuf frames which would be more efficient but require client upgrades. Chose text to minimize customer disruption.
- Depth limit is conservative; for some pipelines (ETL-like) deeper chaining is expected. Plan to expose per-route overrides and safe-listing for enterprise customers.

Telemetry & observability:
- New metrics: tool_chain_length, tool_retries_by_token, signal_stop_reason, shim_transform_rate, injection_conflicts.
- Console: add per-request provenance trace that can expand each frame into the tool run details and PRs/Artifacts.

Security / correctness:
- Result pinning requires canonicalization of outputs before writing to session store (trim whitespace, normalize numeric precision) to avoid near-duplicate tokens.
- security_review_required: true (flagged for KMS/data handling review because some tool outputs may include customer secrets).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end demo: multi-tool chain (3 tools) streams to client with provenance and the console shows correct mapping.
- Recursion scenario tests (unit + integration) cause STOP_FALLBACK and fallback runner invoked deterministically.
- No duplicate injection observed in 10k randomized integration test runs.
- Feature-flagged compatibility shim transforms 99% of legacy outputs in our sample corpus without schema errors.

Rollout plan:
- Merge behind feature flag. Canary on internal Redwood org for 48 hours.
- Canary subset of hosted customers (0.5%) with telemetry monitoring and auto-disable on error budget burn.
- 2-week ramp to default for new customers, enterprise opt-in for older tenants.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Hyperserial+Tool+Bridge
- Implementation RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HyperserialDraft
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus on correctness of idempotency flow and performance of frame parsing in the hot path.
- Pay attention to the default depth/TTL values; propose changes with data.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Streaming frames include provenance and are displayed in console trace. 2) Idempotency prevents duplicate injections in repeated retry scenarios. 3) Recursion heuristics trigger STOP_FALLBACK deterministically in synthetic tests. 4) Compatibility shim converts legacy outputs for >95% of sampled tools. 5) No regression in p50/p95 latency above 5%.
